children: Starwood Capital, the parent of publicly traded Starwood Property Trust
, and Trinitas Ventures have formed a
to develop purpose-built student housing at three major U.S. universities.

The partnership has closed on three sites totaling 2.046K beds serving the University of Pittsburgh, University of Oklahoma, and University of Wisconsin-Madison, with all three projects targeted for delivery in summer 2028.
The projects include 672 beds in Pittsburgh, 677 beds in Norman, Oklahoma, and 697 beds in Madison, Wisconsin.
The developments are located near their respective campuses, where enrollment growth and limited purpose-built housing supply are supporting demand.

The partnership said the projects target markets where student housing supply has not kept pace with enrollment. Purpose-built beds represent only 8% of enrollment in Pittsburgh and 18% in Madison, while Oklahoma's Norman campus reached a record 32.662K students in fall 2025.
The announcement highlights Starwood Capital's institutional capital and investment expertise alongside Trinitas Ventures' integrated development, construction, and property management platform.
Moreover, the stock traded slightly higher at around $15.90 in pre-market trading.
